### Первая волна — Medium

Проведи самостоятельный поиск по веткам с доступной параллельностью. Следи за содержательным покрытием и устранением дублирующихся обзоров. Разные вопросы к одному хорошему первоисточнику допустимы.

Получи подробные материалы каждой ветки. При сбое обозначь точную причину и организуй замену или независимый путь. Отдельный недоступный источник не блокирует всё исследование.

Для критика подготовь исходную цель, карту вопросов, результаты веток и указатели на доказательства. Не передавай предварительное мнение оркестратора как обязательную правильную позицию.

### Критик со свежим контекстом — High

Создай отдельного критика без всей разговорной истории оркестратора. Он получает задание и файлы, оценивает покрытие, доказательность и полезность, ищет пропущенные направления, слабые связи и преждевременные выводы.

Каждое замечание должно указывать конкретную проблему, затронутый материал, последствия для команды, нужное доказательство и задание второй волны. Присвой K001 и далее, сохрани в CRITIC.md.

Критик должен видеть и то, что уже достаточно установлено. Не проси повторно исследовать каждую тему ради видимости независимости. Новое сетевое получение доказательств поручается Medium-исследователям второй волны.

### Вторая волна — Medium

Построй новый набор содержательных задач по критике и неожиданным находкам. В каждую передай K-ID, существующие доказательства, точный недостающий ответ и значение для решения.

Проверяй ключевые рекомендации в том числе через поиск ограничивающих условий и попытку опровержения. Новый агент, повторивший ту же формулировку без нового основания, не добавляет независимого подтверждения.

По завершении сопоставь результаты с критикой: закрыто; уточнена область применимости; обнаружено противоречие; осталось открытым; потеряло значение после новых сведений. Сохрани основания. Это управление второй волной, а не отдельный финальный проверяющий этап.

### Сборщик фактов и источников — High

Отдельный сборщик получает обе волны и критику. Объединяет дубли, восстанавливает происхождение, нормализует идентификаторы и связывает факты с источниками, условиями и противоречиями.

Создаёт SOURCES.md, RAW_FACTS.md, OPEN_QUESTIONS.md и дополняет CRITIC.md результатами обработки замечаний. Подготавливает автору доказательную картину и практические следствия.

Он не усиливает вывод ради стройного рассказа. После двух волн недостающее становится точным открытым вопросом со способом проверки. Скрытая третья волна под видом сборки не нужна.

### Автор — High

Отдельный автор пишет большой связный русский черновик по собранной базе. Сам выбирает подходящую структуру. Объясняет ситуацию, причины выводов, ограничения и действия команды.

Не заполняет пробелы из памяти и не создаёт новый research. Неопределённость, условность рекомендаций и доказательства сохраняются.

### Редактор — High

Отдельный редактор улучшает связность, ясность и читаемость. Убирает канцелярит, повторы и шаблонные конструкции. Сохраняет финальный report_human_<topic>.md.

Может существенно перестроить форму, сохраняя факты, условия, точные литералы и ссылки. Не превращает неизвестное в обещание и не удаляет важное ограничение ради гладкости. Это авторская редактура, а не новый технический аудит.

### Сжиматель машинной версии — High

Отдельный сжиматель получает финальный человеческий текст и доказательную базу. Создаёт английский report_machine_<topic>.md по правилам ниже.

Сохраняет значимое знание и условия, сокращая повторения, повествовательные переходы и длинные общеизвестные объяснения. После сохранения машинной версии передай результаты пользователю. Финального проверяющего не создавай.

## 10. Как искать глубоко и работать с источниками

Ищи ответ по цепочке зацепок. Обнаруженный документ, название, артефакт, автор, версия, внедрение или ошибка могут вывести к более первичному и полезному материалу. Прослеживай такие связи, пока они добавляют понимание.

Подбирай каналы под тему: официальная документация, исходный код, статьи и приложения авторов, первичные измерения, model/dataset cards, материалы внедрившей команды, оригинальные интервью и другие релевантные первичные источники. Список конкретных зацепок задаёт тематический промпт, а исследователи расширяют его по находкам.

Для технических выводов используй первичные документы, код, оригинальные артефакты и измерения. Обзоры, форумы, Habr, публичные соцсети, видео и каталоги могут помогать находить первоисточник. Утверждение из обсуждения остаётся ограниченным своим происхождением, пока не найдено лучшее основание.

Открывай материалы, а не пересказывай поисковые сниппеты. Устанавливай автора, дату, версию и нужный раздел. Для PDF учитывай таблицы, сноски и возможную потерю структуры при извлечении текста; для видео фиксируй таймкод; для кода — commit, путь и функцию; для артефакта — revision и конкретный файл.

Различай дату публикации, дату версии, дату события и дату доступа. Старый подробный документ может быть полезнее новой презентации, но его область применимости должна быть видна. Ссылка docs/stable или latest требует установить фактическую версию при проверке, если это влияет на вывод.

Несколько перепечаток одного пресс-релиза являются одной цепочкой происхождения. Число ссылок не заменяет независимость доказательств. Пригодность источника определяется его содержанием и связью с утверждением.

Ищи по точным сущностям, фразам, параметрам, файлам и версиям. Используй русский и английский, специализированный поиск и другие языки, если есть содержательная причина. Не ограничивайся одним общим запросом по названию темы.

Проверяй реальные возможности среды. Pathfinder или другой поисковый сервис не предполагается. Используй доступные инструменты поиска и чтения; при сбое выбирай другой доступный путь. Недоступный адрес, требование регистрации и ограничение конкретного инструмента — разные наблюдения.

Не описывай закрытый материал как прочитанный. Фиксируй конкретное недостающее звено и продолжай независимые направления. Отсутствие найденного подтверждения не является доказательством отсутствия возможности, документа или объекта.

Сохраняй подробные содержательные выписки и собственный пересказ с локаторами. RAW_FACTS.md не должен заполняться полными копиями чужих страниц. Глубина растёт за счёт найденных сведений и связей, а не объёма скопированного текста.

Не ставь произвольную квоту источников, запросов и примеров. Ветка достаточна, когда даёт полезный ответ или точно локализованное неизвестное после содержательного поиска, а новые поиски перестают менять решения. Продолжай углубление там, где сильная зацепка ещё не разобрана.

## 11. Факты, выводы, доказательства и идентификаторы

Сборщик назначает стабильные локальные идентификаторы:

- S001 и далее — источники;
- F001 и далее — факты и конкретные извлечённые наблюдения;
- K001 и далее — замечания критика;
- Q001 и далее — открытые вопросы;
- E001 и далее — предлагаемые эксперименты, когда они нужны;
- дополнительные идентификаторы сущностей и маршрутов — по необходимости темы.

Во время отдельных веток используй префиксы, например W1-04-S02, затем сохрани их сопоставление с общим реестром. Идентификаторы уникальны внутри исследования. При ссылке на чужой факт указывай topic вместе с ID: одинаковые F-ID в разных папках не обозначают один факт.

В итоговых файлах используй обычные URL и Markdown-ссылки. Не оставляй внутренние ссылки браузера вида turn..., недоступные ссылки на историю чата и временные абсолютные пути своей машины. Относительные ссылки внутри папки должны работать после её переноса.

Различай тип основания:

- заявление производителя, автора или другой заинтересованной стороны;
- конкретное сведение первичной документации;
- наблюдение по исходному коду или метаданным артефакта;
- опубликованное измерение с автором и условиями;
- наше фактическое локальное наблюдение;
- наш вывод из перечисленных оснований;
- предположение для проверки;
- неизвестное.

Тип доказательства и фактический статус проверки — разные признаки. Прочитанный скрипт не равен запущенному скрипту. Сообщение автора об измерении не является нашим экспериментом. Наличие URL не подтверждает получение файла. Предлагаемый тест нельзя записывать как выполненный.

Для значимого утверждения сохраняй источник, локатор, условия, версию или дату контекста, область применения и существенную оговорку. У нашего вывода должны быть короткие понятные основания. Не запрашивай внутренние рассуждения агентов.

Противоречащие сведения сохраняй вместе с условиями. Сначала выясни, относятся ли они к одному объекту, периоду и режиму. Если расхождение не разрешено, не выбирай удобную цифру; сформулируй вопрос и способ проверки.

Не изобретай проценты уверенности. Полезнее показать качество и происхождение основания, независимость подтверждения, фактическую проверку и недостающее звено. Для машинного текста используй компактные единообразные метки с краткой легендой, сохраняя эти различия.

## 12. Содержание четырёх доказательных файлов

# FRESH CRITIC INPUT

This is a neutral file handoff, not a required conclusion. Read both input contracts completely, `PLAN.md`, `RUN_STATE.md`, all fifteen `W1_01.md` through `W1_15.md`, and relevant saved evidence they point to. Original individual tasks are in `AGENT_PROMPTS.md`. Your role instructions are in `ROLE_PROMPTS.md`.

The assigned research question is how to make defensible object/person/event/useful-alert/target-execution claims with reproducible definitions, denominators, unknowns and uncertainty. The supplied folder initially contained no datasets, weights, installed SDK or organizer evaluator. The first-wave results are evidence to examine, not a claim that every recommended protocol is settled.

You are the intermediate critic, not a final report auditor. Do not gather new internet evidence. Write original K-ID criticism with actionable medium second-wave tasks and closure observations. Identify adequate findings too. Distinguish an unknown requiring case/data/device access from a missing public search. The root will schedule second-wave research from your task map; collector will append dispositions without erasing your original critique.

No current model quality or hardware-performance measurements should be inferred from source-level fixtures and mathematical examples. Public LinQ documentation discoveries, access failures and installed/remote-environment unknowns must be examined at their stated scope.
# LATER ROLE PROMPTS

## Fresh-context critic — high

Model `gpt-6.1-sol`, high effort, `fork_turns: none`. Read both input contracts completely, `_WORK/PLAN.md`, `_WORK/RUN_STATE.md`, and every `_WORK/W1_*.md`. You have no parent conversation and must not treat a root opinion as the answer. Do not obtain new internet evidence; formulate missing searches for second-wave medium researchers. Write only `CRITIC.md` and optionally your own `_WORK/CRITIC_HANDOFF.md`. Identify concrete supported coverage and gaps. Each K-ID needs problem, affected cell/facts, engineering consequence, needed evidence, actionable W2 task, closure observation. Preserve initial criticism for later dispositions. Cover object/person/event separation, unknown truth, exact matching/AP, leakage, exposure, few groups, censoring/duplicates, latency survivor bias, async completion, clock domains, coverage and LinQ execution proof. Do not invent weaknesses where existing evidence is adequate. Return prioritized W2 task map.

## Collector — high

Model `gpt-6.1-sol`, high effort, fresh task context. Read contracts, all W1/W2 files, CRITIC and W2 closure map. No new research/network. Own final `SOURCES.md`, `RAW_FACTS.md`, `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`, and append dispositions to existing `CRITIC.md` without erasing original critique. Normalize source IDs S001+, fact IDs F001+, question IDs Q001+, experiment IDs E001+; preserve branch ID mapping in `_WORK/ID_MAP.md`. Source entries: author/title/direct URL/version or pinned commit/publication date versus access date/locator/retrieval status/supporting F-IDs/limitations. Facts: exact observation or own inference, type of basis, actual verification status, source/locator/version/applicability/edge cases/caveats/contradictions. Separate documented rule from our proposal and measured result from future experiment. Avoid a thin narrative substitute for detailed facts. Missing access is not missing capability.

OPEN_QUESTIONS needs prioritized actionable unknowns, searched evidence, why unresolved, affected decision, acquisition route, linked F/K/E. Include eight or more fully specified experiment cards required by topic contract, preferably in RAW_FACTS or OPEN_QUESTIONS and referenced consistently: decision/hypothesis, inputs/access, independent unit, fixed/changed settings, truth and matching, procedure, metrics and exposure, saved artifacts, outcomes, stopping condition, limitation. Give addressed cross-topic handoffs with F/S and next question. Conclude with `_WORK/COLLECTOR_HANDOFF.md` explaining evidence landscape to author. Do not create extra final files, no hidden third wave, no final auditor.

## Human author — high

Model `gpt-6.1-sol`, high effort. Read both contracts and final evidence registries/critic plus collector handoff. No new network or research. Write large, coherent Russian draft `_WORK/AUTHOR_DRAFT.md`. Let the material determine useful structure. Explain causal links through concrete examples, not a metrics glossary: AP versus person association, frame quality versus event matching, balanced precision versus natural exposure, faster graph versus stale queue, zero count versus insufficient evidence. Preserve evidence F/S links, exact versions and mathematical assumptions; all links portable/relative and ordinary direct URLs. No fabricated measured quality, device access or official thresholds. Discuss annotation contracts; alternative event matching and censored episodes; splits, calibration and comparison; rare events and statistics; parity; clocks/load/coverage; minimum harness; experiment cards/routes for 45-hour context; honest claims and addressed handoffs. Explain what works with only images, short clips, unlabelled long video, multiple cameras, late official evaluator, unstable LinQ, demonstration-only data and unobservable PPE. Make report usable to strong team new to topic. Return draft path and editorial guidance. No final human publication until editor.

## Human editor — high

Model `gpt-6.1-sol`, high effort. Read `_WORK/AUTHOR_DRAFT.md`, both contracts and evidence needed to preserve meanings. No network/new research. Improve prose, causal flow and local clarity; remove repetition, bureaucratic language, slogans and false categorical claims. Preserve technical definitions, exact literals, substantive scope/uncertainty, F/S citations, source provenance, unknown versus negative and proposed versus measured. May restructure substantially without adding unsupported facts. Publish `report_human_evaluation.md`; store short change log `_WORK/EDITOR_NOTES.md`. This is editing, not an extra technical audit. No additional final files.

## Machine compressor — high

Model `gpt-6.1-sol`, high effort. Read published human report, both contracts, evidence registries, experiment cards and unresolved questions. No network/new research. Write `report_machine_evaluation.md` in clear compact English. Start valid YAML front matter: topic evaluation, scope, not_covered, answers as actual questions answered in body, keywords, entity_schema null unless a consistent actual recurring record type is used, takeaways, actual checked_at timezone, context_version mosprom-research-v1, evidence/material/access status, actual checks and filenames. No fake tests/date/token counts. Body structure free, search-friendly concrete headings, each section locally understandable with unit/denominator/matching/unknowns/version/limits near conclusion. Significant claims carry evidence-status legend and linked F-IDs. Preserve critical numerical definitions, time boundaries, distinctions between benchmark code, own proposal, mathematical example and measured system behavior. Include usable experiment/routes/handoffs; unresolved answers explicitly link Q-IDs. Can use local lightweight syntax/link checks as part of writing, but do not create a final verification role or stage. On completion save `_WORK/COMPRESSOR_NOTES.md` recording scope of compression and actually performed writing checks, then return file path.

# PLAN — evaluation

The useful output is a reproducible chain from a system claim to observable truth, evaluation unit, matching rule, numerator/denominator, uncertainty and an engineering decision. Object AP, person-state correctness, event usefulness and verified LinQ execution remain separate claims.

## Sequence and ownership

Fifteen independent medium researchers execute in five queues of three. Each reads the common instructions and its individual assignment in `AGENT_PROMPTS.md`, opens primary sources, retains versioned evidence and writes only its own `W1_XX.md` (and its own source subdirectory if useful). The root coordinates and records transitions.

| Cell | Question / decision | Initial evidence route | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 01 | Truth, visibility, unknown and annotation agreement; what can be labeled? | Annotation primary methodology, benchmark annotation policies | W1_01.md |
| 02 | Exact object AP and matching; can two detector results be compared? | COCO evaluator source at pinned commit | W1_02.md |
| 03 | Person–PPE ownership and full-chain evaluation | Primary PPE annotation/evaluation, component oracles | W1_03.md |
| 04 | Zone geometry and boundary truth | Primary geometry APIs and camera calibration | W1_04.md |
| 05 | Temporal event matching, duplicates and censoring | ActivityNet/DCASE/event localization evaluator code | W1_05.md |
| 06 | False alerts and exposure; what does zero establish? | Primary statistical definitions and video event protocols | W1_06.md |
| 07 | Group splits and leakage; what population is tested? | Official split APIs and original leakage studies | W1_07.md |
| 08 | Threshold selection, calibration and abstention | Guo paper, official calibration/threshold docs | W1_08.md |
| 09 | Tracking metrics versus alert continuity | TrackEval code and HOTA paper | W1_09.md |
| 10 | Export/quantization parity; where does behavior change? | Official runtime/export/quantization guidance | W1_10.md |
| 11 | Timing boundaries, clocks and freshness | MLPerf, TensorRT timing guidance, primary clock docs | W1_11.md |
| 12 | Load, drops, availability and coverage | MLPerf loadgen, primary workload/failure accounting | W1_12.md |
| 13 | Small-sample uncertainty and paired comparison | SciPy bootstrap, primary proportion/rate procedures | W1_13.md |
| 14 | Error taxonomy and causal diagnosis | TIDE source/paper, oracle and ablation methods | W1_14.md |
| 15 | Reproducible harness, honest demo, official case/LinQ evidence | Official event site/rules and LinQ pages, evaluator artifacts | W1_15.md |

After all results: prepare neutral handoff → independent high critic writes `CRITIC.md` with K-IDs → medium second wave addresses actual gaps, including attempts to refute key recommendations → high collector writes three registries and dispositions in CRITIC → high author writes Russian draft → high editor publishes Russian report → high compressor publishes English report with valid YAML front matter. No extra final verification role.

## Evidence requirements

Each used primary source: URL, author, publication/version date (or unknown), access time with timezone, locator, commit where code matters, factual retrieval status. Each important observation: branch-prefixed ID, source/locator, actual inspection versus execution, applicability, edge cases, alternative explanation. Own derivations and proposed protocols explicitly identified. Preserve unresolved official data, metrics and LinQ access as actionable questions.

## Final deliverables

`SOURCES.md`, `RAW_FACTS.md`, `CRITIC.md`, `OPEN_QUESTIONS.md`, `report_human_evaluation.md`, `report_machine_evaluation.md`. No global INDEX or extra final report. Experiment cards E-IDs and addressed handoffs live in these files.
# INDIVIDUAL AGENT PROMPTS

## Shared self-contained instructions for every first-wave researcher

You are an independent first-wave researcher, GPT-6.1 Sol (`gpt-6.1-sol`) at medium effort. Working folder: `D:/msk-prom2026-mark/evaluation`. Read this shared section and your assigned cell below; read both input contracts completely if you need fuller context. Team of five prepares for Otkroy#Mosprom 2026, industrial safety video analytics, examples helmet/respirator absence, danger-zone entry, smoking near combustible material. These are examples, not established taxonomy. Inference on LinQ is required by the supplied context; no full case, organizer data/evaluator, SDK, device configuration or access is supplied. RTX 4070 and cloud capability are contextual, no specifications or measured performance assumed. Goal: separate object recognition, person-level violations, useful timely alerts, and verified target execution.

Use available web search/browsing and primary documents/code/papers; open actual sources, do not treat snippets as evidence. You may use network reads through Python/PowerShell for source files and metadata; preserve source provenance, code commit and exact locator. Search beyond seeds when useful; explicitly search for counterexamples and applicability failures. No external messaging, no user questions, no large benchmarks, no application building. Do not spawn more agents. Do not write shared final registries or other cells' files.

Write a substantive standalone Russian or English result `_WORK/W1_XX.md`, UTF-8. Use local IDs `W1-XX-S01`, `W1-XX-F01` etc. Sources must include title, author/org, URL, publication/version date or unknown, access timestamp timezone, section/function, retrieval status and limitations. Facts must separate documentation, source-code inspection, published measurements, locally executed small examples, own inference, proposed protocol and unknown. Record metric units, GT, matching, numerator/denominator, aggregation, ignore/unknown/empty cases, implementation/version, limits. No invented acceptance targets, commands or APIs. Code read is not code run. Preserve contradictions. Paraphrase rather than reproduce long passages. Store any source downloads only in `_WORK/W1_XX_SOURCES/` and keep native names when needed.

At completion give root a short handoff: key findings, decisions affected, output path and unresolved questions. # W1_15 — Reproducible evaluation harness, honest demonstration, official evidence

Research access: 2026-10-23, approximately 06:27–06:31 Europe/Moscow (+03:00). Evidence is public documentation read, not code executed or hardware measured. No SDK installation, compilation, device listing, inference, or model benchmark was performed. All harness requirements below are proposed team protocol, not organizer acceptance rules.

## Findings that change decisions

**W1-15-F01 — Official scope and timing (documentation, S01).** The official landing page dates participation 23–25 October 2026 and advertises 45 hours. Its schedule lists case publication in participant accounts at 13:00 on 23 October, solution upload deadline 10:00 on 25 October, and defenses 12:00–17:30. The 45-hour interval is consistent with publication-to-upload arithmetic, not 45 hours after opening ceremony. The LinQ brief requires model inference on LinQ accelerators and promises participant online access. It describes live camera analysis and immediate notifications, with industrial-safety examples. This public brief does not supply a dataset, evaluator, numerical detection threshold, latency acceptance target, or online endpoint. Do not promote examples into an exhaustive scored taxonomy. Exact local-account updates and full case remain unknown.

**W1-15-F02 — Assessment evidence (documentation, S02).** Regulation §1.4 gives a ten-minute defense allocation: two preparation, five presentation, three questions. §§6.1–6.4 use integer scores 0–3 across prototype functionality, primary problem, development/deployment value, novelty, UX/UI, secondary problems, and analysis. These are jury criteria, not a published AP/FPS formula. §3.6 requires at least one checkpoint with the full team for defense admission, and accessible submission links including code, teaser, demo and presentation; presentation ≤10 MB and accessibility at least 90 working days after results. §1.2 permits demo as video or prototype link. Relevant preparation caveat: §4.1.2 disallows pre-prepared prototype code/material, §4.1.6 mentions public free resources, and §7.3 contains an assistance prohibition. This research is planning evidence, not a determination of how organizers apply those clauses. The team must reconcile allowed preparation/submission practice with organizer instructions. No exhaustive regulation review was undertaken.

**W1-15-F03 — Public executable-path instructions exist (documentation, S06).** The 2025 IVA H1 operator manual, RU.РМДВ.04.06.014-03 34 01, specifies Ubuntu 20.04, ≥32 GB RAM and Python 3.11 (§2.1, printed p5); installation needs a supplied wheel (§2.2, pp5–6). It illustrates ONNX→TensorFlow→quantization→compilation, `.tpu` serialization, then `tpu.Device.list_devices()`, `Device.open`, device `load`, `inference()`, and blocking `inference.sync(...)` (pp19–21). The sample is ResNet-50 classification, not industrial detection. Printed p17 reports `tlm_result.execution_time_us` as TLM estimated execution time; p24's approximately 5627 µs is example output, not this team's measurement. §3.2, p10 warns STAGING can produce invalid programs or compile too long. Tested-network list pp21–22 ends with yolo5s, whereas current tech page lists yolo8/yolo11. Manual Python 3.11 conflicts with software-page Python 3.8 API description. These version scopes require verification. Code was read, not run.

The exact manual link is https://files.lin-q.ru/tpu/docs/Framework_manual_H1.pdf . Page numbering above is printed numbering; corresponding zero-based PDF pages are one less. The document contents calls the instructions §3.3, while the body labels the worked example §3.4 (p11); use page and function locators. Do not infer installed SDK/runtime versions or compatibility from the public example.

**W1-15-F04 — Hardware marketing is not event latency (documentation S03/S04/S08; inference).** `/tech` advertises LinQ H int8 peak throughput and supported families. `/sol` advertises approximately 2.3 ms ResNet-50 latency at small batch, possible optimization to 1.5 ms, PyTorch through ONNX, and Python API/CLI quantization/compilation. The HPS datasheet explicitly says batch=1, names performance tools and developer SDK/support. These do not specify a reproducible full measurement protocol for our model. TOPS, a classifier example, and a named profiler cannot establish live video age, alert delivery, hardware placement, or new model compatibility.

**W1-15-F05 — Access failure is scoped (observed retrieval).** Web open successfully retrieved all four requested pages plus `/docs`, operator manual and HP hardware manual. PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest failed TLS/transport for every attempted download; curl.exe independently failed schannel handshake on the framework PDF. `_WORK/W1_15_SOURCES/retrieval.json` preserves PowerShell failures. This is a local transport failure, not absent public documentation or absent vendor capability. `/docs` has linked documentation, but an installable wheel or hackathon remote endpoint was not obtained. No supplied credentials/device environment were present. Public API documentation is verified; an installed compatible API and executable device access are unverified. This explicitly refines any earlier blanket claim that LinQ execution APIs are undocumented/unavailable.

## Minimal harness contract (W1-15-P01, proposal)

Use one evaluator on immutable prediction artifacts for native/exported/target runs; permit runtime adapters to differ while freezing input and evaluation semantics. Keep runtime failures in the manifest rather than converting them to empty successful predictions. Begin with an auditable small contract, then extend it when actual case/data arrive.

| Artifact | Required content and why |
|---|---|
| `manifest.jsonl` | Clip/frame identifiers; original-byte SHA-256, decoding version, camera/group, split, source/license, image dimensions, frame index, original PTS and timebase, segment start/end, frame-selection rule, expected count, annotation coverage. Re-encoding needs a new identity and link to source. |
| `annotations.jsonl` | Schema/taxonomy revision; person and object geometry; visibility/unknown/ignore; ownership where observable; zone definition and coordinate system; event onset/offset and censored flags; reviewed intervals and adjudication provenance. A missing annotation row must not silently mean safe background. |
| `config.json` | Model/export/compiled-artifact hashes; preprocessing, color/layout/dtype/shape; class mapping; association/NMS/score thresholds; zone anchor/boundary; temporal confirmation/cooldown; batching/concurrency; timeouts and drop policy. Also evaluator source revision and matching policy. |
| `predictions.jsonl` | Raw-output artifact reference when available; detections in declared coordinates; person state/unknown; track IDs; event candidates and delivered alert IDs; score meanings; per-input success/error/drop status. Link outputs to request and input tensor hash. |
| `timestamps.jsonl` | Request/frame ID, clock domain and unit; capture/PTS, ingest, preprocess boundaries, submission, completion, postprocess, event confirmation and delivery acknowledgement. State whether capture is real UTC or file-media time. |
| `run.json` | Run ID; source commit plus dirty patch hash; environment lock/runtime/compiler/driver/firmware/device identity when available; command actually run; seed/determinism settings; start/end and timezone; cold/warm phase; configuration and artifact hashes; stderr/exit status; known limitations. Secrets excluded. |
| `report.json` + rendered table | Metrics with counts, units, evaluator revision and per-stratum denominators; failures and coverage; links to errors and source artifacts. Preserve the machine-readable result even when demo overlays are edited. |

Hashes identify exact bytes; they do not prove annotation correctness, hardware placement or reproducibility by themselves. Canonicalize configuration before hashing, hash every dependency of the result, and retain the original evaluated bytes. A checksum of a rendered video alone cannot identify its model or establish alert accuracy.

## Layers and verification order (W1-15-P02, proposal)

1. **Schema smoke:** validator checks unique IDs, coordinate bounds, finite scores, time order/domain, valid class mapping, complete prediction status, hashes and split membership. A schema pass establishes wiring only.
2. **Evaluator fixtures:** tiny hand-authored expected matches for duplicate detections, wrong class, ignored/unknown person, no positives/no predictions, one alert split into two, two events merged, event already active at clip start, and exact zone boundary. Test numerator/denominator and tie-break behavior, not only final rounded scores.
3. **Diagnostic model regression:** fixed small clips with observable expectations and deliberately hard counterexamples: helmet held in hand, neighboring worker's helmet, hidden head/feet, smoking-like hand motion without observable cigarette, repeated zone entry, track ID switch, sudden camera motion, empty scene, corrupt frame, backend timeout and delayed stale response. No fabricated data is called organizer evaluation. A failure fixture may be a synthetic request failure; label it accordingly.
4. **Parity regression:** identical saved tensors through native/exported/compiled target when available. Compare raw outputs, postprocessed detections/person states and final events separately; localize divergence. Record quantization calibration set and prevent test use for calibration/tuning. A classifier smoke result cannot replace detector/event regression.
5. **Demo:** show a labeled recorded replay or live source, request IDs, frame age, event/alert timeline, measured backend identity status and a failure/recovery example. Mark recorded target output as recorded. Display the same saved report/artifact IDs; never imply cached overlays are current target inference.
6. **Independent evaluation:** freeze model/config/GT and run on previously untouched grouped footage once; report exposure and uncertainty. If no independent split exists, call results diagnostic/dev results. Rerunning demo clips is regression evidence, not generalization evidence.

A useful 45-hour allocation is milestone-based rather than a guessed hourly promise: first executable smoke and schema; then one complete observable violation path with regression; then verified target run/parity; finally freeze, evaluate, package and rehearse. Preserve a submission buffer selected by the team. Do not spend all available time comparing architectures while target execution remains untested.

## Metrics card and accounting (W1-15-P03, proposal)

For every metric supply GT unit, prediction unit, eligibility, matching, threshold, numerator/denominator, aggregation, ignore/unknown policy and empty case. At minimum:

- Object AP only with a pinned evaluator and coordinate/class mapping; do not call it violation precision.
- Person-state recall = correctly identified eligible violation persons / all eligible GT violation persons under full-chain matching. Report missed person detection and unknown coverage separately; an oracle-GT-person experiment is conditional.
- Event precision = matched delivered alerts / eligible delivered alerts; event recall = matched GT events / eligible GT events, under frozen one-to-one temporal/person/class matching. Count unmatched duplicate alerts as false alerts unless contract explicitly declares otherwise. Zero denominator → NA with counts, not perfect score.
- False alerts per evaluated camera-hour = unmatched delivered alerts / fully reviewed eligible camera-hours; list unknown/unreviewed time and do not treat it as negative evidence. Coverage = eligible camera-time successfully analyzed / eligible expected camera-time, with exact treatment of frame sampling and short gaps.
- Host request duration = host completion minus host submission using one monotonic clock; report milliseconds, N, p50/p95 and failures, with warm/cold and batch/concurrency. This includes host/runtime effects inside the boundary, not guaranteed pure device execution. Host remote round-trip is similarly not isolated device time.
- Alert delay requires event observable onset and delivery acknowledgement in compatible clocks; file PTS measures media delay only after an explicit playback mapping. Cross-clock subtraction requires synchronization error bound. Report timeout/missing completion separately; do not erase them from a favorable latency distribution.
- Reconcile expected inputs = successes + failures + drops + unfinished at observation end. For retries use stable logical input ID plus attempt ID to prevent double counting. Report independent sessions/cameras separately before pooled aggregation.

Thresholds/tolerances and service targets require case-owner decisions; none are invented here. Evaluation artifacts may allow another researcher to reproduce arithmetic even if the vendor hardware remains unavailable, but must not label that as rerunning device inference.

## What is sufficient evidence of LinQ execution? (W1-15-P04, proposal/inference)

Maintain an explicit ladder: (a) public API documented; (b) compatible package actually installed/imported; (c) assigned target identified/listed; (d) exact compiled artifact loaded; (e) exact input requests completed with outputs; (f) useful detections/events after parity checks; (g) measured sustained workload with quality/coverage. Current research establishes only (a).

For (c)–(e), preserve organizer-provided endpoint/session identity and version information, target device enumeration or vendor-supported job metadata, compile report, model/tensor hashes, request IDs, full run logs and outputs. If a remote API hides devices, ask for its supported attestation/placement report later; no fictional endpoint or command is supplied here. Backend name in the UI alone is insufficient. Declare CPU/host preprocessing, decoding and postprocessing, and any fallback; “all operations on LinQ” needs operation-placement evidence rather than a successful import or `.tpu` file.

Device-only time requires a vendor-supported timer with a verified boundary and clock. TLM estimates must be stored as estimates in microseconds, never substituted for target measurements. If only client timestamps are exposed, report end-to-end request duration and state isolated device duration unknown. Public manuals and generic supported-network names do not establish custom YOLO operator/export compatibility.

For a five-minute presentation (own proposal informed by S02), prioritize a single traceable violation-to-alert example, one negative/unknown and one recovery example, the frozen metric card and target execution evidence, then limitations. Keep the recording fallback clearly labeled and retain downloadable artifacts. A polished clip demonstrates the displayed path; representative performance requires the independent evaluated corpus and counts.

# W1_05 — Temporal events, alert matching, fragmentation and censoring

Prepared 2026-10-23, Europe/Moscow (UTC+03:00). Scope: reproducible evaluation choices for industrial safety video; no organizer evaluator, full case, event taxonomy, hardware or measured model outputs were supplied. Sources and small examples are in `W1_05_SOURCES/`. This is a proposed local evaluation contract, not a claim about competition scoring.

## Decision supported

**W1-05-F01 — Own inference from inspected sources:** report segment quality and useful delivered alerts separately. A segment can overlap an episode almost perfectly yet start too late to be useful; an immediate, correct notification can have tiny segment overlap. “Event F1” is insufficiently specified without eligibility, temporal rule, assignment, duplicate treatment, operating point and censoring. A detector AP improvement does not establish a reduction in operator interruptions.

Recommended minimal outputs: (1) optional temporal segment AP/tIoU diagnostics, (2) one-to-one timely delivered-alert precision/recall with explicit deadline, (3) latency distribution and late/missed counts, (4) delivered duplicate count and false alerts per evaluated camera-hour, with coverage from W1_06/W1_12. Do not import audio-benchmark collars or tIoU thresholds as industrial acceptance targets.

## Evidence and implementation differences

**W1-05-F02 — Source-code inspection, ActivityNet:** `compute_average_precision_detection` sorts each class's predictions by decreasing score, then considers GT in the same video by descending tIoU. Each GT is locked once per threshold; a prediction uses at most one unlocked eligible GT. Remaining predictions are FP. This is score-ordered greedy assignment, not globally optimal bipartite assignment. Equality to the threshold passes. Recall is cumulative TP / class GT count; precision is cumulative TP / cumulative predictions. Wrapper macro-averages AP over GT-derived classes and then thresholds (default ten thresholds 0.50–0.95). No predictions returns AP zero. Label vocabulary comes from GT subset; an unknown prediction label triggers mapping failure. Same class, wrong person is not distinguishable by these fields. [Pinned evaluator](https://github.com/activitynet/ActivityNet/blob/82304fa9f4a7219421df13dae6347a445c4cf5bc/Evaluation/eval_detection.py#L182) [W1-05-S01].

**W1-05-F03 — Source-code inspection, ActivityNet utility:** tIoU is intersection duration / union duration, where intersection is clamped to zero. It is unitless if all timestamps use the same unit; use seconds in our schema. AP integrates a monotonic precision envelope at recall changes. Thus two identical predictions for one GT produce TP then FP, but AP can remain 1.0: the extra FP arrives after recall has already reached 1.0. A single AP number therefore need not expose duplicate burden. These formulas assume positive, valid interval durations; point alerts should not be represented as zero-duration segments and passed to this metric. [Pinned utilities](https://github.com/activitynet/ActivityNet/blob/82304fa9f4a7219421df13dae6347a445c4cf5bc/Evaluation/utils.py#L14) [W1-05-S02].

**W1-05-F04 — Source-code inspection, sed_eval:** collar validity uses `abs(pred_onset - ref_onset) <= t_collar`; offset validity uses `abs(pred_offset - ref_offset) <= max(t_collar, percentage_of_length * reference_duration)`. Default onset and offset checks are enabled, collar 0.2 seconds, relative offset tolerance 0.5. `optimal` forms same-label valid edges and performs one-to-one matching; `greedy` is retained. Each file is evaluated separately, and counts accumulate. Classwise FP = Nsys − Ntp; FN = Nref − Ntp. Overall error-rate accounting also separates substitutions, so its FP/FN fields should not be silently treated as classwise unmatched counts. [Pinned source](https://github.com/TUT-ARG/sed_eval/blob/0cb1b6d11ceec4fe500cc9b31079c9d8666ed6eb/sed_eval/sound_event.py#L1108) [W1-05-S03].

**W1-05-F05 — Source-code inspection and documentation:** sed_eval's utility implements maximum-cardinality bipartite matching, not “first eligible” matching; tied maximum matchings need not minimize delay. Documentation explicitly warns that greedy matching can depend on GT order. The metric helpers return NaN precision when Nsys=0 and NaN recall when Nref=0; `empty_system_output_handling='zero_score'` can override empty-system precision. Record and report empty strata rather than silently averaging only defined scores. [Matching code](https://github.com/TUT-ARG/sed_eval/blob/0cb1b6d11ceec4fe500cc9b31079c9d8666ed6eb/sed_eval/util/event_matching.py#L7), [metric helpers](https://github.com/TUT-ARG/sed_eval/blob/0cb1b6d11ceec4fe500cc9b31079c9d8666ed6eb/sed_eval/metric.py#L31), [API docs](https://tut-arg.github.io/sed_eval/generated/sed_eval.sound_event.EventBasedMetrics.html) [W1-05-S04/S05/S06].

**W1-05-F06 — Official benchmark documentation:** DCASE is not one fixed temporal rule. DCASE 2017 Task 2 specifies onset-only evaluation with 0.5-second collar; DCASE 2020 Task 4 specifies 0.2-second onset and max(0.2 seconds, 20% of reference duration) offset collars. These differ from the library's default 50% offset tolerance. A symmetric onset collar accepts a prediction slightly before reference onset; that is boundary agreement, not automatically a valid causal early warning. ## Proposed industrial alert contract (W1-05-P01; own proposal)

The contract below is for useful delivered notifications. Freeze its parameters before test; organizer rules, if supplied, remain a separate result.

1. **GT episode:** `episode_id, camera_id, violation_type, person_instance_id (or explicit identity-unavailable), zone_id if relevant, observable_start, observable_end, onset_status, offset_status, onset_uncertainty, evaluated_support, annotation_version`. Use half-open state intervals [start,end). Define what makes two episodes distinct: e.g. observed safe exit/reset followed by a new entry. A gap caused by an occlusion is not automatically a safe reset. Distinguish actual continued violation from inability to observe it; this requires truth policy from W1_01/W1_04/W1_09.
2. **Raw candidate versus delivered alert:** retain `candidate_id`, evidence frame timestamp, predicted support interval, confidence, confirmation timestamp, `logical_alert_id`, delivery attempt ID, delivery timestamp/status and stream epoch. Candidate suppression, logical alert creation, transport retries and UI delivery are different layers. Count every actual extra operator interruption in workload; retries collapsed idempotently into one visible notification remain one delivery, with retry logs retained. Candidate-only metrics must be named accordingly.
3. **Compatible keys:** same camera, violation, zone and correct person when the task is person-specific. Matching by model track ID alone is invalid; track IDs can switch. If person correspondence cannot be annotated, report a separately named scene/zone alert result, not person-alert precision. For zone-wide alerts about simultaneous people, define an actionable group GT beforehand.
4. **Timely edge:** alert delivered at `t_delivery` is eligible for episode g when `0 <= t_delivery - observable_start(g) <= D_type` and delivery occurs while the episode is observably active (end boundary excluded). Deadline D is an explicit application requirement, currently unknown. Any allowed pre-onset tolerance for annotation uncertainty must be separately declared; it should not silently authorize predicting future violations. A warning-after-episode policy, if wanted, needs another named rule. For uncertain onset intervals, report bounded delay/sensitivity rather than falsely precise latency.
5. **Assignment:** maximize number of eligible one-to-one pairs; among equally large matchings minimize total nonnegative delay, then resolve ties by stable episode/alert IDs. This is our deterministic offline proposal. It is not ActivityNet's greedy rule or sed_eval's latency objective. Never allow one delivery to clear several independently actionable GT episodes. For audit, save eligibility edges, final pair list and reason for each unmatched item.
6. **Count:** TP = matched delivered alerts; FN = eligible, fully evaluable GT − TP; FP = unmatched evaluable delivered alerts. `P=TP/(TP+FP)`, `R=TP/(TP+FN)`, `F1=2TP/(2TP+FP+FN)`. Decompose unmatched deliveries: duplicate of already notified episode, correct-but-late, wrong person/type/zone, no GT, uncertain/unreviewed. Late is outside timely TP and therefore contributes FP plus an unmatched GT FN in this strict endpoint; also report eventual episode detection separately so the interpretation is clear. Duplicate is an FP subtype, never an extra TP. Unknown/ignored deliveries are counted separately and do not establish correctness.
7. **Aggregation:** sum counts over evaluated streams for micro P/R/F1; report per violation, camera and duration stratum as well as any explicitly defined macro average. GT episode is recall unit, delivered alert is precision unit. Units of delay are seconds; ratio scores unitless (or percent, clearly marked). Empty denominators → undefined with raw counts; do not call all-negative empty clips perfect recall. All-negative fully reviewed clips still contribute unmatched alerts/workload/exposure. No duration/threshold averaging without specifying weights.
8. **Latency:** report every eligible episode's timely/missed status alongside TP delay quantiles and number of samples. Quantiles among detected episodes alone can improve when slow episodes are missed. Retain confidence-threshold and temporal-policy configuration (dwell, smoothing, exit hysteresis, gap tolerance, cooldown, rearm rule), versions and timestamps. Choose these on development data; test output is locked.

## Episode lifecycle, cooldown and censoring (W1-05-P02; own proposal)

**Repeated entry and cooldown:** GT [10,14] then [16,20] are two episodes if a qualifying safe exit is observed. A 10-second cooldown suppressing the second delivery produces FN under that task. Do not merge GT to fit the cooldown. Conversely, if state stays unsafe through a short occlusion and only a tracker ID changes, a re-alert is a duplicate, not a new GT. Scope cooldown to defined keys; a scene-wide cooldown can suppress another worker's new violation. Reminders/escalations need a separate output type and utility endpoint; retain them in the delivered interruption count even when the product intentionally requests them.

**Left censoring/pre-existing episodes:** observation starts at 0 while actual episode began at −10. Annotate `onset_status=pre_existing_or_unknown` and observable unsafe state at 0. Do not label 0 as true onset or claim ten-second physical-onset latency. Measure a separate startup/pre-existing-state notification endpoint from first sufficient observable evidence. Segment metrics on the clipped [0,30] support can be perfect yet physical onset detection remains unknowable.

**Right censoring:** GT begins at 28, file stops at 30, D=5 s. A run ending at 30 cannot demonstrate what would be delivered by 33. Mark deadline-followup incomplete and report count; do not automatically call no alert a full-window miss. If delivered at 29, observed timely success is known, but mixing such successes with excluded no-alert cases biases recall. Primary complete-window recall should exclude the entire right-censored eligibility stratum consistently, and report its partial observations separately. A separate “detected before recording end” endpoint can score all such episodes with its shorter opportunity explicitly named. Prefer longer continuous recordings when possible.

**Unobservability, cut clips and reconnects:** unknown video intervals and delivery-outage intervals are distinct. A hidden unsafe person is not evidence of a safe exit. Store episode continuation ID across adjacent cuts; avoid double-counting one episode in two clips. Reconnect creates a stream epoch and possible left-censored state; do not fabricate onset. For segmentation scoring, visible GT may be clipped to evaluated support, but original censor flags persist and onset/offset localization results exclude unknown boundaries. Fully observed early episode endings are real task conditions, not censoring; our active-episode delivery criterion intentionally gives them less response opportunity.

**Four clocks:** physical true onset may precede observable sign; first observable sign precedes or coincides with sufficient annotation evidence; algorithm confirmation after dwell is an algorithm timestamp; delivery is when notification becomes available at the defined receiving boundary. Example: physical 8, observable 10, confirmation 12, delivery 15 → observable-to-delivery 5 s, confirmation-to-delivery 3 s, physical-to-delivery 7 s only if physical onset is independently known. Backdating prediction start to 10 does not make a delivery at 15 instantaneous. Clock-domain reconciliation belongs to W1_11.

## Open requirements and handoff

No justified D, onset/offset collars, minimum dwell, cooldown, reset gap, identity annotation coverage or notification-delivery boundary is available. These are requirements to fix, not values to discover in a sound benchmark. Need organizer GT/evaluator and domain owner's episode policy to determine official comparability. W1_01 must supply unknown/observable-state semantics; W1_09 person continuity; W1_06 camera-hour and duplicate workload; W1_11 clocks; W1_12 coverage/dropouts. Alert matching must not hide these unknowns with one generic “F1”.

# W1_04 — Danger-zone geometry and boundary semantics

Research date: 2026-10-23. Result for violation_methods / video_architecture. No organizer zone definition, camera data, calibration, target SDK or device execution was supplied. No acceptance threshold is established here.

## Decision in one paragraph

Adopt an explicit **observable zone-membership contract before calling it physical danger-zone entry**. A polygon in a frame, a person's ground contact, and any part of their body entering a hazardous volume are different targets. Fix the polygon coordinate system, anchor definition, boundary inclusion, visibility/unknown policy and zone version. Keep raw per-frame membership separate from temporal confirmation and delivered alerts. A correct point-in-polygon implementation establishes conformance to that declared geometry; it does not establish physical hazard truth. For a floor-zone case, use independently annotated ground-contact/foot evidence where observable, and mark unresolved contacts unknown. Treat bottom-center of a detection box as an explicitly tested proxy rather than a physical fact. These are proposals, not supplied organizer rules.

## Evidence and exact API behavior

**W1-04-F01 — Documentation plus source inspection.** OpenCV's `pointPolygonTest(contour, pt, false)` distinguishes interior (+1), exterior (-1), and edge/vertex (0); `true` returns signed distance to the nearest contour edge. Thus `r > 0` excludes boundary; `r >= 0` includes boundary. Distance is in the supplied coordinate units, e.g. pixels for pixel coordinates, not automatically metres. The frozen 4.12.0 header states the contract; `geometry.cpp` implements it [W1-04-S01]. In its integer branch lines 117–146 and floating branch 161–190, the implementation checks edge/vertex contact and uses odd/even crossing counts. Inspection is not execution. A single contour is not a shell-plus-holes data model: implement declared hole semantics separately or select a polygon API supporting holes.

**W1-04-F02 — Documentation.** For a point, Shapely 2.1.2 `contains(zone, point)` excludes the boundary, whereas `covers(zone, point)` includes it [W1-04-S02, S03]. Do not generalize this into “contains always excludes every boundary contact of an arbitrary second geometry”: a line with endpoints on the polygon boundary can still be contained when its interior lies inside. `contains(zone, zone)` is true. A footprint predicate must be specified independently from a point predicate. Missing inputs can return false, so validate missingness before interpreting booleans as outside.

**W1-04-F03 — Source inspection, failure case.** In OpenCV 4.12.0 `geometry.cpp` lines 103–112, contour vector shape and depth are asserted, and an accepted zero-length contour returns -1, or -DBL_MAX with distance enabled [W1-04-S01]. The numeric answer must not silently turn a missing zone into normal “outside.” Reject invalid/missing zone configuration upstream. There is no user-selected geometric tolerance in this API; floating comparisons and coordinate precision are part of behavior. Source inspection found no general polygon validity certification in this function. Reject self-intersecting/degenerate input through the application's validity contract instead of treating a numeric result as approval of geometry.

# W1_05 — Temporal events, alert matching, fragmentation and censoring

Prepared 2026-10-23, Europe/Moscow (UTC+03:00). Scope: reproducible evaluation choices for industrial safety video; no organizer evaluator, full case, event taxonomy, hardware or measured model outputs were supplied. Sources and small examples are in `W1_05_SOURCES/`. This is a proposed local evaluation contract, not a claim about competition scoring.

## Decision supported

**W1-05-F01 — Own inference from inspected sources:** report segment quality and useful delivered alerts separately. A segment can overlap an episode almost perfectly yet start too late to be useful; an immediate, correct notification can have tiny segment overlap. “Event F1” is insufficiently specified without eligibility, temporal rule, assignment, duplicate treatment, operating point and censoring. A detector AP improvement does not establish a reduction in operator interruptions.

Recommended minimal outputs: (1) optional temporal segment AP/tIoU diagnostics, (2) one-to-one timely delivered-alert precision/recall with explicit deadline, (3) latency distribution and late/missed counts, (4) delivered duplicate count and false alerts per evaluated camera-hour, with coverage from W1_06/W1_12. Do not import audio-benchmark collars or tIoU thresholds as industrial acceptance targets.

## Evidence and implementation differences

**W1-05-F02 — Source-code inspection, ActivityNet:** `compute_average_precision_detection` sorts each class's predictions by decreasing score, then considers GT in the same video by descending tIoU. Each GT is locked once per threshold; a prediction uses at most one unlocked eligible GT. Remaining predictions are FP. This is score-ordered greedy assignment, not globally optimal bipartite assignment. Equality to the threshold passes. Recall is cumulative TP / class GT count; precision is cumulative TP / cumulative predictions. Wrapper macro-averages AP over GT-derived classes and then thresholds (default ten thresholds 0.50–0.95). No predictions returns AP zero. Label vocabulary comes from GT subset; an unknown prediction label triggers mapping failure. Same class, wrong person is not distinguishable by these fields. [Pinned evaluator](https://github.com/activitynet/ActivityNet/blob/82304fa9f4a7219421df13dae6347a445c4cf5bc/Evaluation/eval_detection.py#L182) [W1-05-S01].

**W1-05-F03 — Source-code inspection, ActivityNet utility:** tIoU is intersection duration / union duration, where intersection is clamped to zero. It is unitless if all timestamps use the same unit; use seconds in our schema. AP integrates a monotonic precision envelope at recall changes. Thus two identical predictions for one GT produce TP then FP, but AP can remain 1.0: the extra FP arrives after recall has already reached 1.0. A single AP number therefore need not expose duplicate burden. These formulas assume positive, valid interval durations; point alerts should not be represented as zero-duration segments and passed to this metric. [Pinned utilities](https://github.com/activitynet/ActivityNet/blob/82304fa9f4a7219421df13dae6347a445c4cf5bc/Evaluation/utils.py#L14) [W1-05-S02].

# W1_06 — Rare events, false delivered alerts, and evaluated exposure

Research date: 2026-10-23; access timezone UTC (Moscow = UTC+03:00). Scope: evaluation design for industrial safety video analytics, not measured performance of any model or LinQ. No organizer evaluator, continuous deployment data, delivered-alert log, or annotation contract was supplied. No acceptance threshold is inferred. This cell proposes a protocol and gives mathematical examples, not an operational workload guarantee.

## Decision supported

A defensible workload statement needs the count of actually delivered notifications, their adjudicated status, and the camera-time over which those notifications could have occurred and been evaluated. “Zero false alerts” without duration, coverage, review status, fixed configuration, and population is not a rate claim. Reviewing only alert clips can establish alert correctness on those clips; it cannot establish missed-event recall. A long quiet-camera recording is weak evidence for a busy unseen camera even when the arithmetic camera-hours is large.

Evidence labels below: **DOC** = primary documentation/paper; **DERIVATION** = mathematical consequence under stated model; **PROPOSAL** = our evaluation rule, not an existing benchmark requirement; **LOCAL MATH** = arithmetic executed locally without video/model; **UNKNOWN** = missing task evidence. No evaluator code was inspected or executed in this cell.

## Primary evidence and applicability

**W1-06-F01 / DOC, S01.** TRECVid 2008 uses spurious event observations divided by processed camera-hours (section 2.4.2). It explains why an ordinary true-negative event count is problematic for events with arbitrary onset and duration. Its data comprise five synchronized cameras over multiple days (section 2.2), and its retrospective task allows multiple video passes (section 2.1.1). Thus this is a relevant continuous-surveillance precedent for an exposure denominator, but does not certify live delivery, latency, current industrial event truth, or our chosen duplicate rules. The source itself warns that camera-hour false-alarm rate differs from a Type-I error probability because target observations are included in the denominator.

**W1-06-F02 / DOC, S02–S03.** NIST's constant HPP/exponential model estimates occurrence rate by count / total operating time, and supplies a zero-failure one-sided bound. Scholz derives exact conservative Poisson mean bounds by inverting tail probabilities; the zero-count 95% upper mean is 2.995732. These are model-conditional statistical results, not evidence that video false notifications follow that model.

# W1_08 — Operating points, calibration and abstention

Prepared 2026-10-23. Scope: industrial video analytics evaluation; no organizer evaluator, target data, LinQ SDK/device configuration or measured model output was supplied. Examples below are proposed contracts and mathematical counterexamples, not measured project results. Source IDs and evidence types are explicit. No acceptance targets are inferred.

## Decision in one paragraph

Select and freeze the **whole delivered-alert policy** on development/validation data independent at the deployment-relevant camera/video/session grouping. Model checkpoint, preprocessing, candidate cutoff, NMS, person association, tracker, calibration, class thresholds, temporal confirmation, unknown handling and cooldown jointly determine that policy. Report held-out person/event recall, timely recall, delivered false alerts per evaluated camera-hour, latency and coverage alongside object metrics. A classifier probability calibrated for one population/unit is not automatically a probability that a timely, correctly associated event alarm is useful. Calibration helps interpret a specified score; it does not specify the operational tradeoff or repair unseen events.

## Supported findings

**W1-08-F01 — Published classification result, not a video guarantee.** Guo et al. define confidence calibration through correctness conditional on confidence; their ECE weights binwise absolute confidence–accuracy gaps by bin occupancy. They fit positive scalar temperature T on validation logits via NLL, using softmax(z/T); this preserves the within-example argmax. Their experiments concern image/document classification. They report temperature scaling often effective, with a Reuters exception; this is not a theorem of calibration on a new camera or event pipeline. [W1-08-S01, §§2, 4.2, 5]

**W1-08-F02 — Documentation.** Scikit-learn separates estimating scores from deciding actions. `TunedThresholdClassifierCV` selects a threshold to optimize a chosen scorer; default balanced accuracy is a software default, not an industrial objective. Its default stratified fivefold CV does not encode camera/session independence. `cv='prefit'` requires separate threshold-tuning validation data rather than reuse of classifier training data. The positive class and scorer parameters must be explicit. [W1-08-S02, §§3.3.1–3.3.1.2]

**W1-08-F03 — Documentation.** A calibrator must see predictions independent of base-model fitting; otherwise confidence is biased. Scikit-learn's CV calibration avoids that fitting reuse, but the caller must choose appropriate folds. Absent classes in training or calibration folds produce problematic probability/calibrator behavior. Brier/log loss combine calibration with discrimination and outcome uncertainty, so a lower loss alone does not establish better calibration. [W1-08-S03, §§1.16.1–1.16.3]

# W1_09 — Tracking continuity versus useful safety alerts

Research completed 2026-10-23; access window 03:16–03:22 UTC (06:16–06:22 Europe/Moscow, UTC+03:00). Scope: primary papers, pinned TrackEval source, four tiny evaluator examples. No industrial dataset/model benchmark, device test, or proof of LinQ execution was performed.

## Decision and evidence boundary

**W1-09-F01 [own inference from S01–S06].** Track quality and alert quality require separate evidence. HOTA/IDF1/MOTA evaluate detections and their association to annotated trajectories; they do not read PPE ownership, violation state, alert delivery, cooldown or episode semantics. Good tracking can support temporal policies but cannot certify them. A tracker ID is a sequence-local token; it does not establish an employee’s name, badge identity, legal identity, or even cross-camera identity. An event ID and a track ID should be distinct fields.

**W1-09-F02 [documentation/paper].** HOTA explicitly separates detection and association; its paper demonstrates failure modes of prior metrics, including MOTA’s emphasis on detection and IDF1’s global trajectory matching behavior. These are metric-design results on MOT tasks, not measurements of industrial alert performance. Ristani et al. explain that identity-based and event-based tracking measures answer different user questions; their “event-based” CLEAR errors are tracking decisions, not delivered safety-alert episodes. [S01, S06]

## Inputs and scope of identity truth

**W1-09-F03 [source inspection; proposed annotation contract].** The metric routines consume aligned frame lists `gt_ids`, `tracker_ids`, pairwise similarity matrices and totals of IDs/detections/timesteps. The MOTChallenge adapter reads frame, ID, x/y/width/height, GT mark/class or tracker confidence; it computes box IoU, remaps IDs to contiguous indices, and rejects duplicate IDs within a frame. Preserve stable GT person IDs across every interval where annotators can establish continuity; tracker numeric IDs need not equal GT numeric IDs. GT has to identify which person is which, independently of predictions. [S02–S05]

Proposed minimum record: `sequence_id, camera_id, frame_index, source_timestamp, gt_person_id, bbox, annotation_status, visibility, identity_link_status`. Add `episode_id, violation_type, observable_state, onset/end bounds` for alert evaluation, and `pred_track_id, state_owner_id, emitted_alert_id, delivery_timestamp, reset/transfer_reason` in predictions/logs. These extra fields are our proposal, not TrackEval inputs. Specify whether IDs persist across complete occlusion, exit/re-entry, a file boundary, camera restart or camera change. Uncertain linking must be recorded as uncertain, not guessed to obtain a score.

# W1_10 — Native, exported, quantized and target-compiled parity

Research cutoff: 2026-10-23, approximately 03:23 UTC / 06:23 Europe/Moscow (UTC+03). Assignment: industrial-safety video analytics; LinQ inference required by supplied context, but no SDK, device configuration, model or access supplied. This is a research result and proposed test contract, not a measured deployment result. Code was inspected, not executed for inference. No model, LinQ compiler or target benchmark was run.

## Decision and principal findings

**Keep four separate claims:** (1) artifact is structurally accepted; (2) numerical outputs agree within a declared contract; (3) application quality and alert behavior remain acceptable; (4) the named target actually executed the declared workload. Evidence for one does not establish the next. Establish the native baseline, then isolate export, compiler/runtime, quantization and application changes in paired stages. The task owner must approve task-level degradation limits; the deployment owner must establish actual device placement. No universal epsilon, mAP loss allowance or LinQ command is justified by available evidence.

- **W1-10-F01 — documentation:** Floating-point operation ordering, platform and batching can change outputs without a software defect. Bitwise agreement is not a default cross-runtime criterion, even for FP32. PyTorch v2.5.1 explicitly documents this; archived TensorRT 10.x troubleshooting agrees. A reproducibility requirement within one pinned environment is a separate question. [W1-10-S01, S08]
- **W1-10-F02 — code inspection:** Preprocessing can differ before either network runs. Ultralytics v8.3.0 provides an unusually useful counterexample: `pre_transform` makes `LetterBox(auto=same_shapes and self.model.pt, ...)`; therefore native `.pt` and non-`.pt` paths can use different padding even with the same `imgsz`. Its `preprocess` normalizes non-tensor images by 255 and converts BGR/BHWC to RGB/BCHW, but a tensor input bypasses those image-path operations. A parity test must compare actual tensors, not assert that filenames and resolution settings match. This is a version-specific example, not a recommendation to adopt Ultralytics. [W1-10-S03]
- **W1-10-F03 — code inspection/documentation:** NMS is a semantic boundary. ONNX NMS-11 has boxes `[batch, boxes, 4]`, scores `[batch, classes, boxes]`, a format attribute, per-class output cap and selected-index output. Its default cap of zero produces no selected boxes. Ultralytics' inspected NMS consumes another layout, applies strict `>` confidence filtering, class handling and a global retained-detection cap. Substituting one for the other requires an explicit adapter. [W1-10-S05, S04]
- **W1-10-F04 — documented counterexample:** Equal-score overlapping boxes need not produce the same selected box on Torchvision CPU and GPU. Output-array equality can fail while both obey that API. Sort-order changes must be distinguished from missing/extra detections and from changed selected geometry. [W1-10-S06]
- **W1-10-F05 — documentation/code inspection:** Quantization is lossy. Static calibration estimates activation parameters from calibration inputs; parameter choices and hardware arithmetic matter. The ORT debugging code can expose and match activations, but its `collect_activations` defaults to CPU and disabled graph optimization. Running it unchanged would not demonstrate compiled LinQ behavior. [W1-10-S07, S09]
- **W1-10-F06 — documentation plus inference:** ORT can partition a graph among execution providers and use CPU for nodes unsupported by a higher-priority provider. Thus registered providers and successful inference are insufficient proof of full accelerator placement. This is a concrete ORT failure mode supporting a general evidence requirement, not evidence that LinQ uses ORT or permits fallback. [W1-10-S10]
- **W1-10-F07 — own inference:** Small tensor error is neither necessary nor sufficient for identical alerts. Thresholding, NMS, association, zone boundaries and temporal state introduce discontinuities. Conversely, nearly identical application metrics can conceal serious failures on rare event classes. Report both paired behavior differences and ground-truth quality.

# W1_12 — Joint load, failure, availability and camera-time coverage accounting

Checked: 2026-10-23, UTC (+00:00); precise retrieval times are in `_WORK/W1_12_SOURCES/retrieval.json`. Scope: proposed evaluation contract for industrial safety video analytics, including required LinQ inference. No hardware, LinQ SDK, running application, dataset or official acceptance targets were supplied. No load benchmark or application code was executed. English standalone research note.

## Decision and evidence status

**Decision:** every quality result needs its workload, missing-work ledger, exposure and freshness next to it. Fewer false alerts alone cannot establish improvement when less camera-time was analyzed. A request-success fraction and a fast latency percentile cannot establish video coverage or timely warnings.

Evidence labels used below: **DOC** = primary published documentation; **CODE** = source read at an immutable revision, not executed; **INFERENCE** = reasoning from explicitly stated assumptions; **PROPOSAL** = our evaluation convention, not an official contest or vendor standard; **UNKNOWN** = unresolved access/configuration/ground truth.

## Primary findings, with applicability failures

- **W1-12-F01 — DOC, S01:** MLPerf distinguishes Single Stream (next query after previous completion), Server/Interactive (Poisson arrivals), Offline (all samples issued initially) and Multistream (queries with eight samples, next query after completion). Its latency starts at scheduled query time, not merely actual dispatch. **INFERENCE:** closed-loop completion-driven tests reduce offered work when the system slows; they do not reproduce independent camera arrivals. MLPerf's term Multistream is a benchmark query pattern, not proof of eight independently paced video decoders. Its prescribed durations/percentiles are benchmark rules, not acceptance targets for this case.
- **W1-12-F02 — CODE, S02:** `ScheduleDistribution<TestScenario::Server>` uses exponential interarrival times; the response path records completion latency from `scheduled_time` and traces scheduling delay separately from issue-to-done time. `IssueQueries` flushes queries and obtains expected completion latencies before deriving active duration. This supports keeping delayed issue and tail completion visible. It does not provide a video truth/coverage protocol or prove arbitrary application failures are safely handled.
- **W1-12-F03 — DOC, S03:** LoadGen is model/data-format unaware and does not score output accuracy itself. The user must return completion for each received sample and assess the accuracy log. This clarifies an apparent simplification in the rules' description of LoadGen as responsible for validating accuracy: the framework supplies traffic/logging, while the task-specific scorer remains necessary. Our camera-time/event evaluator must therefore be explicit.
- **W1-12-F04 — DOC, S04:** Triton exposes successful/failed requests, inference samples and batch executions as different counts. A request may contain multiple samples; cached requests are excluded from inference/execution counts. Its pending gauge covers backend-waiting work, not all front-end activity or executing work. Failure categories include scheduler rejection, cancellation, backend and other errors. Ensemble/component failure counts can overlap. **INFERENCE:** do not sum per-model counters into unique user transactions, infer complete end-to-end success from backend success, or interpret zero pending as no outstanding work. These are examples of accounting boundaries, not a recommendation or assumption that LinQ uses Triton.
# W1_13 — Small samples, uncertainty and paired comparisons

Prepared 2026-10-23; research access around 03:27–03:33 UTC (06:27–06:33 Europe/Moscow, UTC+03:00). Scope: evaluation methodology for industrial safety video analytics, with no organizer dataset, evaluator or measured system outputs supplied. All numbers below are mathematical examples or locally executed calculations on invented arrays, **not model tests**. No acceptance threshold or universal minimum sample size is proposed.

## Decisions supported

1. Define the target population and independent sampling unit before choosing an interval. Thousands of adjacent frames from one incident do not provide thousands of independent incident trials. For claims about new cameras, count independent cameras/sites, not just episodes or frames.
2. Compare frozen systems A and B on the same truth, video, exposure and matching policy. Resample whole independent groups jointly for both systems and recompute the difference. `paired=True` in SciPy preserves corresponding indices; the caller must make those indices represent the independent groups.
3. With very few groups, give raw counts, per-group results and leave-one-group-out sensitivity. A bootstrap interval can describe sensitivity to the observed groups; it does not by itself justify a nominal population coverage claim.
4. Zero observed failures require a nonzero uncertainty bound under explicit binomial or Poisson assumptions. An ordinary bootstrap on all zeros cannot discover an unobserved failure.
5. Separate sampling uncertainty, run/seed variability, selection optimism, annotation uncertainty and domain uncertainty. Increasing bootstrap draws only reduces simulation noise conditional on the same data.

## Evidence register and methodological limits

**W1-13-F01 — Documentation, SciPy bootstrap [S01].** The current documentation rendered as SciPy 1.18.0. Its API exposes paired index resampling, percentile/basic/BCa intervals, sample axis, number of resamples, and an RNG. Defaults include 9,999 resamples, unpaired samples and BCa. It warns that degenerate data may produce undefined BCa bounds. The RNG keyword changed in 1.15.0; new code should use `rng`. None of these options identifies video dependence or selects a cluster structure.

# W1_14 — Error diagnosis and causes of improvement

Checked: 2026-10-23, approximately 06:25–06:35 Europe/Moscow (UTC+03:00). Actual per-download UTC timestamps and SHA256 are in [retrieval.json](W1_14_SOURCES/retrieval.json). Scope: evaluation research for industrial-safety video analytics; no organizer dataset, official evaluator, LinQ SDK/device access, or measured system outputs supplied. Helmet/respirator/zone/smoking examples do not establish the complete task taxonomy.

## Decision and evidence status

Use two connected records: **what observable output went wrong** and **what evidence supports a cause**. A missing alert is an outcome; “detector failed” is a hypothesis until upstream input, annotation, association, temporal policy and delivery are checked. Prioritize fixes with paired full-chain outcomes and component interventions, while preserving conditional oracle results separately.

Legend: DOC = primary documentation/paper method; CODE = inspected source, not executed; PUB = authors' published result; LOCAL = executed mathematical illustration; PROPOSED = our evaluation design; INFERENCE = our conclusion; UNKNOWN = unavailable evidence. No TIDE, detector, tracker, export or LinQ benchmark was run. Python has numpy, but pycocotools was absent; there was no dependency installation. Downloading and inspecting code does not constitute reproducing the paper.

## Primary findings

**W1-14-F01 — DOC; TIDE is an output-error diagnostic.** TIDE partitions detection errors into classification, localization, both, duplicate, background and missed GT. Its oracle score is ΔAP = AP after fixing one category minus baseline AP. Each category starts from the same baseline; progressive fixes change apparent importance with order. Missed-GT repair reduces the GT count rather than inventing a confidence for a new detection. These are metric counterfactuals, not deployable repairs. The paper uses foreground/background IoU thresholds; defaults are 0.5/0.1. See [S01](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.08115v2), §2.2–2.3 and appendix B.1–B.2.

**W1-14-F02 — CODE; pin the executable definition.** Inspected TIDE commit `49a5d2a4aeb56795e93a3ed7cc7e6d25757bb4c1`, version 1.0.1. In `quantify.py`, `TIDEExample._run` sorts predictions by score, caps the image list by `max_dets`, and greedily matches same-class GT at IoU ≥ positive threshold, marking GT used. `TIDERun._eval_image` checks Box, Class, Duplicate, Background, then Other; ignored predictions may participate in error analysis. `fix_main_errors(progressive=False)` separately repairs categories and clips negative ΔAP to zero. Exact-threshold cases need fixtures: its Box branch includes both endpoints (`bg_thresh <= IoU <= pos_thresh`) and precedes Duplicate. For an already-used same-class GT at exactly the positive threshold, this can select Box rather than Duplicate. This is a code-reading observation, not an executed counterexample. [S02](https://github.com/dbolya/tide/blob/49a5d2a4aeb56795e93a3ed7cc7e6d25757bb4c1/tidecv/quantify.py#L198).
